gen-flavors-gf-noto-sans-tai-le: Whimsical and a bit bossy, Flavors stacks towering lowercase with diagonals as hefty as its stems. Noto Sans Tai Le is the quiet one, a plain sans whose strokes taper off before they touch.
gen-gf-autour-one-gf-noto-sans-thai-loop: Autour One pulls its strokes like solder through a nozzle, each round letter fed by a clear channel into the curve. Noto Sans Thai Looped gives it tall, sturdy-looking lowercase.
gen-gf-funnel-display-gf-noto-sans-yi: Funnel Display draws spaghetti-like strokes with the line weight of a technical pen, and its c tips never creep toward closing. Noto Sans Yi adds a deep midsection.
gen-gf-goldman-gf-parkinsans: Round forms like open parentheses give Goldman its stance, with widely set letters and a lowercase that towers over its capitals. Parkinsans keeps one stroke thickness throughout, crisp even when shrunk.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-puritan: Cut-out, chunky, and tall in the lowercase, Gugi looks like it was routed from a slab. Puritan, a plain sans, counters with rounded forms and oversized e and a counters, while Gugi saves its punch for the headline.
gen-audiowide-gf-noto-sans-lisu: Futuristic through and through, Audiowide sets tall lowercase like tiles with wide grout lines, horizontals as thick as verticals. Noto Sans Lisu has wide-open s curves, so give it room.
gen-gf-offside-gf-sofia-sans: Offside spaces its letters widely and leaves its curves refusing to close, a level beat with no accents of weight. Sofia Sans stands tall like cut acrylic stencil pieces, so a long passage moves along smoothly.
gen-gf-oxanium-gf-sen: Sen reads modern and tall, with a line of constant weight tracing each letter. Oxanium shares that big lowercase and monoline stroke, and its curves end in clear daylight, which is what ties them.
gen-gf-paprika-gf-sono: Sono reads tall and widely spaced, a plain sans whose lowercase a keeps its mouth ajar. Paprika scatters its letters at a distance, and both fonts breathe in the same way.
gen-gf-revalia-gf-sofia-sans-semi-conden: Wide, bold, and loose-limbed. Revalia strides across separated letters, while Sofia Sans Semi Condensed answers with a sans-serif built from strips of equal width, its lowercase nearly matching the capitals.
